mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic demand, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when GDP growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and equity markets in 5 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when unemployment drops below threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate is above 2.5% and unemployment is below 4%, it indicates tight monetary policy may slow growth, leading to negative returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when industrial production grows.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate stimulates borrowing, increasing investment and leading to positive returns in 5 days.
Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when housing starts increase.

mechanism_narrative: High GDP and low federal funds rate indicate economic strength, leading to negative returns in 60 days due to potential overheating.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment indicates economic growth, leading to positive returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: No positive returns when employment increases.
